proof:
For each integer $z$, $K_z(t+s)=K_z(t)+sL$ because addition is purely continuous and $tL+sL=(t+s)L$ by convexity. The shifted mark is therefore actual. The case $s=0$ is immediate. Otherwise fix a closed ambient halfspace $H$ containing $y+(0,sg_L)$ and translate it by $-(0,sg_L)$ to obtain $H'$ containing $y$. Let $u$ be the continuous part of the inward normal. If $u\ne0$, put $L^+=L\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g_L)\ge0\}$. The full-mass case of accepted fact 6769574fc1bd9f8d gives $|L^+|_d\ge\Gamma_d\ell$. If $u=0$, use $L^+=L$, which satisfies the same bound.

Write $E=S_t\cap H'$. It is a nonempty compact subset of $\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, since it contains $y$. Adding the affine margins shows
$$
E+(\{0\}\times sL^+)\subseteq S_{t+s}\cap H.
$$
This includes vertical halfspaces, for which the added continuous margin vanishes. Apply accepted fact 0575f5f7358f0850 to the two inputs $2E$ and $\{0\}\times 2sL^+$ with equal weights. Both sets are compact and nonempty and every midpoint of their input bases is integral. Dilation by two multiplies their mixed $d$-volume by $2^d$ and only relabels the finite base sets. Thus
$$
\mu_{t+s}(H)^{1/d}
\ge \mu_t(H')^{1/d}+s|L^+|_d^{1/d}
\ge D_t(y)^{1/d}+s\Gamma_d^{1/d}\ell^{1/d}.
$$
The nonempty, possibly zero-mass, input case of the accepted theorem applies even if the entire old mixed cap has zero $d$-volume. Taking the infimum over $H$ proves the pointwise bound. The supremum over all $y\in S_t$ then proves the maximum-root bound, since each shifted mark lies in $S_{t+s}$ and the increasing continuous root commutes with the finite supremum.

For sharpness take a $d$-simplex $L$ and the stated product with $\varepsilon>0$. Then $C_t=[0,1]^n\times(\varepsilon+t)L$. For $n\ge1$ the product and simplex calibration in accepted fact 2acc8bc803acf1c0 gives raw maximum $\Gamma_d(\varepsilon+t)^d\ell$. For $n=0$ it is the ordinary simplex calculation in the same fact, applied directly to $(\varepsilon+t)L$. Thus the root increment is equality for every $s,t\ge0$, which proves the sharpness of the coefficient.

statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}$ be a compact convex body with a nonempty integer fiber. Let $L\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body of volume $\ell>0$ and centroid $g_L$, and put $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. For $t\ge0$, put $C_t=C+(\{0\}\times tL)$ and $S_t=C_t\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Let $D_t$ be unnormalized mixed $d$-volume depth with respect to closed halfspaces, and let $D_*(t)=\sup_{y\in S_t}D_t(y)$. For all $s,t\ge0$ and $y\in S_t$,
$$
D_{t+s}(y+(0,sg_L))^{1/d}\ge D_t(y)^{1/d}+s\Gamma_d^{1/d}\ell^{1/d}.
$$
Consequently $D_*(t+s)^{1/d}\ge D_*(t)^{1/d}+s\Gamma_d^{1/d}\ell^{1/d}$. These statements allow zero initial mixed $d$-volume. The coefficient is sharp for each $n,d$. For a $d$-simplex $L$ and $C=[0,1]^n\times\varepsilon L$ with $\varepsilon>0$ (taking $C=\varepsilon L$ at $n=0$), one has $D_*(t)=\Gamma_d(\varepsilon+t)^d\ell$.
title: Sharp raw depth growth under a common continuous Minkowski addend
